title: Repeated sibling elements: only the last one is kept
body: In `xmltodict.py`, `xmltodict.parse` should turn repeated sibling elements into a list, but only the last element survives: ```python >>> xmltodict.parse("123") {'a': {'b': '3'}} # expected {'a': {'b': ['1', '2', '3']}} ``` Expected: two or more siblings with the same name become a list in document order (also when they contain child elements or attributes); a single element stays a scalar unless `force_list` says otherwise.
provenance: upstream code at a pinned commit with an injected regression; the oracle is the unmodified upstream file

source.modifications: reformatted with black (layout and quote style only) to pass the repository formatting check; snapshot adds the injected defect, visible tests and empty package markers

defect: A second sibling with the same key overwrites the first instead of making a list.
